links.outcome: Male-female diagnostic performance gap and equalized odds difference after fairness-aware model design
links.effect: Male-female performance gap reduced from 15.42% to 1.75%; equalized odds difference 0.0423, below the 0.10 acceptance threshold.
links.quote: The male-female diagnostic performance gap is reduced from 15.42% to 1.75%, with an equalized odds difference (EO) of 0.0423-well within the clinical acceptance threshold of 0.10.

links.outcome: Effect of fairness regularization on subgroup disparity and overall accuracy
links.effect: Gap reduced from 15.42% to 1.75% while macro F1 0.8952 and AUROC 0.9762 surpassed all baselines.
links.quote: Evaluated on PTB-XL (21,507 recordings), DA-GAT-v2 achieves macro F1 of 0.8952 and AUROC of 0.9762, surpassing all compared baselines.

unlisted_practices: Demographic-conditioned architecture (FiLM, dynamic graph topology) for ECG fairness
Curriculum training with composite fairness regularization loss

screen.reason: The paper develops and benchmarks a new deep learning architecture (DA-GAT-v2) for 12-lead ECG interpretation with a focus on mitigating demographic bias (algorithmic fairness), evaluated on benchmark datasets (PTB-XL and Chapman-Shaoxing).
